Passive Voice Highlighter

Find likely passive-voice constructions in your writing with a regex highlighter — "was written", "has been taken" and more.

Heuristic highlighter: a form of "be" + past participle (-ed/-en ending or a known irregular like "written"). Review each hit — adjectives such as "was tired" can be false positives.

📖 How to use

  1. Paste your text into the box.
  2. Likely passive constructions (a form of "be" + past participle) are highlighted in yellow.
  3. Click any highlight count to jump through matches; rewrite flagged spots in active voice.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How does the detection work?

It finds a form of "be" (am, is, are, was, were, be, being, been) followed by a past participle — a word ending in -ed/-en or a known irregular participle like "written" or "taken".

Is it always right?

No. It is a fast heuristic, not a grammar engine: "was tired" is an adjective use, not passive. Use the highlights as prompts to review, not as verdicts.

Why avoid passive voice?

Active voice is usually shorter and clearer: "The team shipped the update" beats "The update was shipped by the team". Some passive use is fine and intentional.
